noetic-sample-g7-01.title: Try the number of groups of 5
noetic-sample-g7-01.body:
We need $4a + 5b = 31$ with whole numbers $a, b$.

- $b = 1$: $31 - 5 = 26$, not a multiple of 4.
- $b = 3$: $31 - 15 = 16 = 4 \times 4$ ✓
- $b = 5$: $31 - 25 = 6$, no. ($b$ must be odd because 31 is odd; $b = 7$ is too big.)

So 4 groups of 4 and 3 groups of 5: $4 + 3 = 7$ groups.

**Answer: 7 groups**

noetic-sample-g7-01.title: Bound the number of groups
noetic-sample-g7-01.body:
If there are $n$ groups, the number of people is between $4n$ and $5n$.

- $n = 6$: at most 30 people — too few.
- $n = 7$: between 28 and 35 — possible. With all groups of 4 we'd have 28; each group changed to a 5 adds 1, so 3 groups of 5 give 31 ✓
- $n = 8$: at least 32 — too many.

So there are exactly 7 groups.

**Answer: 7 groups**

noetic-sample-g7-02.title: Simplify each balance
noetic-sample-g7-02.body:
Let $A$, $B$, $P$ be the weights of one apple, banana and pear.

- First fact: $2A + P > 2B + P$, so $A > B$.
- Second fact: $2P + B > 2A + P$, so $P + B > 2A$, i.e. $P > A + (A - B)$. Since $A - B > 0$, $P > A$.

So banana < apple < pear.

**Answer: (B)**

noetic-sample-g7-02.title: Test the choices
noetic-sample-g7-02.body:
From the first scale (remove one pear from each side), an apple is heavier than a banana. That rules out (A).

- (C) and (D) say the apple is the heaviest. Then $2A > P + B$ (two apples beat any pear-plus-banana), contradicting the second fact $P + B > 2A$.

Only (B) is left: banana < apple < pear. Check with $B = 1, A = 2, P = 4$: $2A + P = 8 > 2B + P = 6$ ✓ and $2P + B = 9 > 2A + P = 8$ ✓

**Answer: (B)**

noetic-sample-g7-03.title: Look at the end first
noetic-sample-g7-03.body:
The total stays 42. At the end Nancy has twice as many as Mary, so Mary has $42 \div 3 = 14$ and Nancy has 28.

Mary kept 70% of her crayons, so 70% of her original amount is 14. Then 10% is 2, and 100% is 20.

**Answer: 20 crayons**

noetic-sample-g7-03.title: Equation
noetic-sample-g7-03.body:
Let Mary start with $m$. She keeps $0.7m$; Nancy ends with $42 - 0.7m$.

$42 - 0.7m = 2(0.7m) \Rightarrow 42 = 2.1m \Rightarrow m = 20$.

Check: Mary gives 6, keeping 14; Nancy has $22 + 6 = 28 = 2 \times 14$ ✓

**Answer: 20 crayons**

noetic-sample-g7-04.title: Two squares plus two triangles
noetic-sample-g7-04.body:
The squares have sides $\sqrt{25} = 5$ and $\sqrt{144} = 12$.

The hexagon is made of the two squares and two right triangles:

- Triangle $BPC$: legs $BP = 5$ and $PC = 12$, area $\frac{1}{2} \cdot 5 \cdot 12 = 30$.
- Triangle $FPE$: legs $FP = 5$ and $PE = 12$, area $30$.

Total: $25 + 144 + 30 + 30 = 229$ in².

**Answer: 229 in²**

noetic-sample-g7-04.title: Big rectangle minus corners
noetic-sample-g7-04.body:
Put the figure in a box: it spans $5 + 12 = 17$ across and $5 + 12 = 17$ down, so the box is $17 \times 17 = 289$.

The parts of the box outside the hexagon are:

- top right: the region above $BC$ — a right triangle with legs 12 and 5 (area 30);
- bottom left: the region left of $FE$ — a right triangle with legs 5 and 12 (area 30).

$289 - 30 - 30 = 229$ in².

**Answer: 229 in²**

noetic-sample-g7-05.title: Each switch is worth 8 points
noetic-sample-g7-05.body:
If all 10 were wrong, he'd have $-30$ points. Changing one answer from wrong to right adds $5 + 3 = 8$ points.

He needs $10 - (-30) = 40$ more points: $40 \div 8 = 5$ correct answers.

**Answer: 5 questions**

noetic-sample-g7-05.title: Equation
noetic-sample-g7-05.body:
Let $c$ be the number correct. Then $5c - 3(10 - c) = 10$, so $8c - 30 = 10$ and $c = 5$.

Check: $5 \times 5 - 3 \times 5 = 25 - 15 = 10$ ✓

**Answer: 5 questions**
